summary: Yawen Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Yang earned an MA from Fo Guang University, studying under supervisor Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).

Yeshe Thupten worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught Daniel Cozort, Donald S. Lopez Jr., and Joe Bransford Wilson, and held appointments as a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia (1982) and Middlebury College (1982).

Yeshi Dhonden (1927–2019) was a specialist in Tibetology. He studied at the Chakpori Institute of Tibetan Medicine under Khyenrab Norbu. In 1961, he founded Men-Tsee-Khang, serving as its director from 1961 to 1966.
Yi-hsun Huang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. Huang earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner and later taught Huidi Zeng.

Yifa (born 1959) works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned degrees from National Taiwan University, University of Hawaiʻi, and Yale under Stanley Weinstein. She served as department head and dean at University of the West (~1996–2004) and founded Woodenfish Foundation.

Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1988–1994) and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock (~1994–1999). He held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~2007).

Yijie Tang (1927–2014) worked in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Peking University (~1947–1951), he served there as a professor (~1956–2014), held a post at Stanford (~1990–1991), and founded the International Academy of Chinese Culture.

Yiliang Zhou (1913–2001) worked in history, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Fu Jen Catholic University, Yenching University, Harvard University, and under Yinke Chen (~1935–1939). From ~1952 to 2001, he served as a professor at Peking University.

Yin Shun (1906–2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Minnan Buddhist Academy, Wuchang Buddhist Institute, and Taisho University. He taught at Minnan, Wuchang, Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute, and directed Fawang Buddhist Institute, later presiding over the Hong Kong Buddhist Association.

Ying-shih Yü (1930–2021) was a scholar of Sinology, history, and philosophy. Educated at Yenching, New Asia College, CUHK, and Harvard (PhD 1962), he held professorships at Harvard, CUHK, Yale (1977–1987), and Princeton University (1987–2001).

Yingguang Qu (1883–1973) was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School (~1904–1907) and under teachers including Nordan Hutuktu, Bai Puren, Nona Hutuktu, and Gangkar Rinpoche, later teaching Shek-wing Tam and Yui Chi Lau.

Yinke Chen (1890–1969) was a historian, Sinologist, and linguist. Educated abroad, including at Berlin, Harvard, and under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Heinrich Lüders, he held professorships at Tsinghua, Peking University, Academia Sinica, and Sun Yat-sen University.
Yirmiyahu Yovel (1935–2018) was a philosopher. He was educated at the Hebrew Reali School, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1957–1968), and Princeton University (~1966–1968).
Yiu Wing Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Chan earned a PhD from The University of Hong Kong by 2013, supervised by K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yoel Hoffmann (1937–2023) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tel Aviv University, Hanazono University, and Kyoto University (PhD), and served as a professor of philosophy, Buddhism, and Japanese poetry at the University of Haifa (~1978–2003).

Yohei Kawajiri is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. Kawajiri served as a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013) and as an extraordinary researcher for the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011).

Yoichi Fukuda (born 1955) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a senior researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003 and 2015).

Yoneo Ishii (1929–2010) was a scholar of history, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Chulalongkorn University. He served at Kyoto University (~1965–1990), Sophia University, as director of CEACS (~1995–2001), and as president of Kanda University of International Studies (~1997–2004).
Yong Hua is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Hua completed a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2014).

Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak (born 1926) is a Tibetology and religious studies scholar. Trained at Menri and other monasteries, he founded Menri and Triten Norbutse monasteries, serving as lopön at both, and held visiting scholar posts at SOAS (1961) and Munich (1969).
